questions.stem: How is the structure of capillaries adapted for the exchange of substances with tissues?

options.text: They have thick muscular walls to push substances out
They have valves to control the direction of substance movement
They have walls only one cell thick, providing a short diffusion distance
They have elastic fibres that stretch to release substances

questions.explanation: Capillary walls are only one cell thick (endothelium), creating the shortest possible diffusion distance for oxygen, carbon dioxide, nutrients, and waste products to move between the blood and surrounding tissues.
